distinguishing_features: Passive SLIPS coating on wellbore screen and casing, not an operational agitation change
Lowers critical adhesion shear stress below operating wall shear, rather than increasing shear stress
Applied to geothermal reinjection well surfaces to prevent silica scale adhesion
No additional hardware or operational changes; passive mechanism
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent silica scale adhesion on geothermal reinjection well surfaces to maintain injectivity without periodic cleaning or operational changes
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism is physically sound: operating wall shear (3.28 Pa) exceeds the SLIPS critical shear (<1 Pa), and the test protocol can validate it.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The prior art teaches increasing shear stress via agitation, not reducing critical adhesion stress via a passive surface coating; applying SLIPS to geothermal wellbores to lower critical shear below operating shear is a non-obvious mechanism.
